The video begins with a shot of a man walking directly toward the camera, positioned beneath a large, white, catamaran hull under construction in a warehouse-type environment. He's wearing a light t-shirt with the image "Ruby Rose Sailing Est. MMXXI" printed on it, and light jeans. He's gesturing as he speaks to the camera, indicating progress on the boat build. The camera transitions to a shot from inside the catamaran, looking out through the door area, where a seating area and partial kitchen are visible. The interior is still under construction, with protective plastic coverings. The camera transitions back to the man, who is now standing directly in front of the catamaran, still speaking enthusiastically. He gestures with his hands, and the focus tightens on him. Finally, the video transitions to a blue background, where a water splash effect forms the logo "RR2 London Sun & Sea" with an image of a boat.

MMXII" (Ruby Rose Sailing EST. 2012) in a stylized logo. The man gestures with his hands and talks directly to the camera, with a positive and energetic expression. Workers wearing yellow protective clothing are visible in the background, engaged in various tasks on wooden tables and other construction materials. The setting is an industrial indoor space, possibly a shipyard or a workshop, filled with construction equipment and materials. The man explains he wants to show some features beneath the boat, particularly the escape hatches. The camera then pans to show a fixed, non-opening window, described as a "break glass in case of emergency" type escape hatch. Then, there's a quick shot of the back of the catamaran with a dinghy attached, and a man sitting on the stern. The man continues speaking, and the camera returns to the underside of the boat, completing the tour.

The focus is on the underside of the portside hull, and the camera zooms in on what is identified as the lightning protection system, which consists of a pair of ridged metal components. A man with a light beard then appears in the center of the frame in front of the boat. He is wearing a light-colored t-shirt and gesturing with his hands as he speaks. He tells the viewer he will go onto the boat and describe it from his perspective as he does so. He climbs the stairs to access the boat. He removes his shoes and we see that there are many pairs of similar black shoes lined up neatly on the steps. He appears curious and is then winkingly back to the camera to continue his tour.

The video segment showcases a man in a gray t-shirt emblazoned with "Ruby Rose SAILING" in red text pointing out the engine fire port on a boat. He gestures with his hands, explaining that the port is there so that in case of an engine fire, one can insert the nozzle of a fire extinguisher through the port instead of opening the engine hatch. The man explains that the point is not to feed the fire by opening the engine hatch. The boat is mostly white and appears to be in a hangar with scaffolding surrounding it.

The video opens with a view from the deck of a white catamaran under construction. A gray inflatable dinghy labeled "Highfield" sits on the deck. The camera pans around the interior of the cockpit, revealing a man in a gray "Ruby Rose Sailing" t-shirt with a logo. He is the primary focus as he walks around the cockpit area, explaining the setup of the tender, winch, and steering, gesturing with his hands to indicate their positions. He also points out what appears to be the forward seating section. The video cuts to a wide exterior shot of the catamaran from the dock, and then returns to the man as he continues the tour, pointing out design elements and discussing the placement of seating and equipment. The environment is a large, industrial shipyard with other boats in various stages of construction visible in the background. The camera movements are mostly handheld, following the man as he talks and gestures.

The scene takes place inside the partially constructed interior of a white catamaran. A man wearing a grey T-shirt with the words "Ruby Rose Sailing" walks toward the camera, explaining the advantages of the boat's bench seat, including its suitability for smaller individuals, its size for two, its forward and backward orientation, its comfort during passage, and its good visibility. He gestures frequently as he speaks, emphasizing his points. In the background, we see workers in yellow hard hats, various tools and equipment, and the interior elements of the boat, such as seats, windows, and countertops, some of which are covered in protective plastic. The camera then pans to show a wider view of the interior, including more of the boat's furnishings and windows, offering a glimpse of the shipyard outside. The man then backs into the boat.

The video features a middle-aged man with short hair, wearing a grey t-shirt with the text "Ruby Rose SAILING EST. MMXXI", moving boxes inside a boat interior, specifically the kitchen area. He is addressing the camera, asking not to tell someone named James that he is moving things. He points out various features such as the galley, cabinetry, sink, tap, and electronic windows, emphasizing the size and airiness of the space. There is a refrigerator. He lies down on a sofa, commenting on how comfortable and nice the boat is. He is interrupted by a Vietnamese worker, who looks at the man strangely. The video also presents the boat exterior, which is a white catamaran.

The video segment begins with a shot of the exterior of a boat, with its rear window open. The camera transitions inside, revealing a cluttered interior with cardboard boxes, tools, and the boat’s steering wheel. A man with short, dark hair and a gray t-shirt then lies down on a mattress, speaks to the camera, and then sits up. He proceeds to highlight the boat’s interior features, such as light switches and a sweeping dashboard covered in tape. He also points out opening windows and the quality of the cabinetry. Later in the video, he introduces a camera light, intending to illuminate the boat’s walk-in wardrobe design. The man highlights various elements of the wardrobe’s construction, particularly the quality of the woodwork and craftsmanship. Throughout the segment, he expresses his enthusiasm about the boat's interior design and the high-quality workmanship.

The video begins with a man in a gray "Ruby Rose Sailing EST. MMXX" t-shirt, sitting on a cushioned seat inside a boat, addressing the viewers with hand gestures and expressive facial expressions. He discusses the quality of "joinery" (a nautical term for the carpentry of boat interiors) in catamaran construction, challenging viewers to post images of the joinery in their own boats. The camera pans to show the yacht's interior, highlighting the wooden cabinetry and trim details, and showing its open windows and ventilation system. The presenter notes that the quality of joinery can be an indicator of overall boat quality. He challenges his viewers to send in photographs of their joinery work, and tags the Sailing Ruby Rose site. The camera shows the view from the helm onto the deck, and beyond that the water, and also shows an exterior shot of the boat inside its covered construction site. The segment concludes with a logo animation for "RR2 London Sails & Rigs" over a dark blue ocean scene.
